blocks.title: MATCHING CHOICE:
blocks.text: Greedy per-order is simple and low-latency. Batching every 2-5 s with the Hungarian algorithm gives better global cost.

items: ==Ingest== rider GPS from 300K riders
Compute the **ETA** for every active order
Show the live map and status to the customer
300K riders pinging every 5 s = ==60K writes/sec==
Pings go to Kafka; Redis keeps only the latest location
Push over WebSocket or SSE; **poll** every 10 s as fallback
Fan-out is per order: a rider has 1-3 watchers
GPS drops in tunnels: **interpolate** and snap to roads
Gateway restart: clients reconnect with backoff
On reconnect, pull the latest snapshot via GET

Sampled history to S3 keeps hot storage cheap

blocks.q: Q1. How do you avoid double charges?
a_bullets: Idempotency key per attempt; unique `(order_id, attempt)`

blocks.q: Q2. A rider goes offline mid-delivery?
a_bullets: Heartbeat expires the 60 s location TTL
Reassign from last order state; notify new ETA

blocks.q: Q3. Scale for a cricket-final dinner peak?
a_bullets: Pre-scale before the match, not after
Shed recommendations, cache hot menus, shard hot city, protect order path

blocks.q: Q4. How do you keep search results fresh?
a_bullets: CDC from catalog DB into Elasticsearch
Live is_open overlay; cached city listing fallback

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Be strict on orders and payments, loose on search and tracking.

caption.text: An end-to-end system design case study of a Zomato/Swiggy-style food delivery app. It covers scale estimates, architecture, search, orders, cart, payments, delivery assignment, live tracking, notifications, and a closing cheatsheet of scaling, failure handling and interview questions.
